items.quote: So, to answer your question, will the ESOP cost reduce? Yes, dramatically, yes.

items.statement: Non-cash charges were INR 46 crores in the quarter versus zero last year.
items.quote: Non-cash charges, INR46 crores.

items.statement: Net flows were INR 4,186 crores, up 39% year-on-year, highest ever.
items.quote: The highest net flow ever in the history of Anand Rathi Wealth of the last 20 years happened in this quarter, which went by, and we collected new fresh moneys of INR 4,186 crores, which is up 39% from the last year's number, corresponding number, of FY26 quarter ending September.

items.statement: Equity mutual fund net flow was INR 2,867 crores, up 39%, highest ever.
items.quote: Second, we recorded our highest ever quarterly equity mutual fund net flow, again, in the last 20 years we have not been able to achieve that, and with your support and client support, we have achieved INR 2,867 crores, up 39%.

items.statement: Net flows split: 62% existing clients, 38% new clients.
items.quote: Now, coming to the exact number for the last quarter, 62% is existing, 38% is new, sir.

items.statement: Primary MLD issuance INR 2,073 crores and secondary INR 750-odd crores in the quarter.
items.quote: Primary INR 2,073 cores.

items.statement: Mutual fund license application to be filed by month end.
items.quote: This month end we applied for mutual fund license application.

items.statement: GIFT City operations expected in a couple of months with two funds.
items.quote: Yes, sir, so in the couple of months, not too far. And two funds.

items.statement: Added 1,500 net new client families, total 14,309; attrition 0.17% in Q2.
items.quote: In our flagship business of private wealth, during the last 12 months, we have added 1,500 new client families on the net basis, bringing our total client families to 14,309.

items.statement: Digital wealth AUM grew 14% to INR 2,531 crores; clients up 15% to 7,584.
items.quote: Digital wealth business, which is B2B2C business, registered an AUM growth of 14% year-on-year and reached INR 2,531 crores, and the number of clients increased 15% to 7,584.

items.statement: Expects MTF book to add INR600-700 crores quarterly and continue growing.
items.quote: But what we are seeing is on average we are able to add like INR600 crores, INR700 crores on a quarterly basis. Our expectation is that trend should continue.

items.statement: Plans to spend INR400-500 crores annually on cost to grow, with flexibility.
items.quote: I think we've been talking about that roughly we spend between INR400 crores to INR500 crores a year. And in a good year, obviously we'll end up spending INR500 crores plus as well.

items.statement: Next quarter cost to grow may exceed INR125 crores if market does well, or be lower if not.
items.quote: But next quarter, if market does well, we will probably spend more than that as well. But if market doesn't do well, we might do lower than that as well.

items.statement: Expects cash and F&O market share to converge with NSE active market share over long term, possibly 10 years.
items.quote: I think probably it will take 10 years to reach to those numbers, but it will converge one day, which might be like infinity in some ways.

items.statement: Expects MTF as percentage of cash turnover to increase in foreseeable future, but not necessarily every quarter.
items.quote: I think, we expect at least in the foreseeable future that number will kind of go up. But again, percentage of ADTO can vary also.

items.statement: Employee cost structurally will go up, not come down from here.
items.quote: So, there's a short-term blip, but structurally the cost is going to go up.

items.statement: Cost to serve increased due to AI costs, compute costs, more trading days, and one-time INR10-13 crore hit.
items.quote: Because of these three things, the Cost to Serve went up, and Cost to Grow went down because of IPL not being there in this quarter.

items.statement: UPI MDR implementation expected not to materially change cost, but depends on final number and capping.
items.quote: Our expectation is it's not going to be a material change to our cost in any case, but obviously it will depend on how much actual number that comes out to be.

items.statement: Cash brokerage per order is closer to INR15-16, while equity derivatives and commodities are INR20 per order.
items.quote: So, if you look at our brokerage income per order on cash side is actually more closer to like INR15, INR16 compared to in equity derivatives and commodities where per order it's INR20.

items.statement: CAS normalization expected to be faster from applicable date, but depends on date.
items.quote: We think that from the date it becomes applicable, the normalization will be much fa ster. But it will depend on from which date it becomes applicable

items.statement: US stocks product early testing, feedback good, no timeline for full launch.
items.quote: As for the US stocks, it's kind of very, very early. Just kind of started testing the water. The feedback is really good from the customers.

items.statement: More than 50% of customers use more than two products, and more than 5% use more than four products.
items.quote: So, I think, broadly, more than 50% of our customers are today using more than two products, and actually more than 5% are using more than four products today.

items.statement: Wealth management AUM disclosed; MF Prime small but fastest-growing; Fisdom users included in active customers.
items.quote: Because MF Prime is very small, I think you can assume that it's not a significant part of it yet. But obviously, that's probably the fastest-growing part at the same time.

items.statement: MTF policy strengthened with real-time execution and industry-level book monitoring, higher haircuts on some stocks.
items.quote: And we are actually sitting in some cases like 80% as haircut, which effectively means that we are only fun ding 20% in that

items.statement: Other operating income boosted by 30 IPOs in quarter and BSDA revenue.
items.quote: So, this quarter had we have seen about 30 IPOs happening in this quarter. And some of the large IPOs, in fact, happened this quarter, which includes your SBI AMC, NSE.

items.statement: 915 power trading product not yet significant contributor to volume or revenue.
items.quote: Basically, the 915 is not a significant contributor to the trading volume today. And we obviously, our expectation is that the day we get a -- like a significant PMF on that product, it will start contributing significantly, and the m arket share can grow even faster

name: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Ltd

items.statement: Total ESOP cost for this financial year expected between 64 to 68 crores, charged pro rata to P&L.
items.quote: On the ESOP cost, we've indicated that the total ESOP cost for this financial year would be between 64 to 68 crores. So accordingly, the charge happens to the P&L on a pro rata basis, so that guidance continues.

items.statement: Alternate business net yield expected in range of 90 to 95 basis points.
items.quote: See, I think we indicated in the last call as well, you should see the yield in the alternate in a range between net yield between 90 basis point to 95 basis point.

items.statement: Alternate yields broadly expected in range of 90 to 100 basis points.
items.quote: On a broad basis, what we've experienced from the past that the yield range has been between 90 to 95 or maybe 90 to 100 , that's the range between which the alternate yields have largely been.

items.statement: SIF yields clubbed with equity yield; 67 basis point equity yield includes SIF.
items.quote: No. So, 67 basis point yield would include SIF. We would categorize as Nimesh mentioned, for all practical purposes, SIF is pretty much like equity AUM, except for the minimum ticket size. So, SIF yields have been clubbed with the equity yield.

items.statement: PMS business from ICICI Securities has approximately near to INR3,000 crores of AUM to be migrated after approvals.
items.quote: The business of ICICI Securities in the PMS comprises of discretionary, non -discretionary, and non-binding advisory services. We see about approximately near to INR3,000 crores of AUM.

items.statement: Four SIF strategies live with AUM; debt category will continue to be explored and launched at appropriate time.
items.quote: We've already got four strategies which we have which we are live and where we have AUM. These are equity long -short, hybrid asset allocator, and as well as ex -Top 100. Insofar as debt category is concerned, we will continue we'll continue to explore.

items.statement: Planning to launch a fund with 51% plus invested in private space and remainder in public space.
items.quote: We have come with a category where 51% plus will be invested in the private space, and the remaining can get invested in the public space. So that is another mix that we think that we are ready to offer in the market and we are launching that kind of fund.

items.statement: No plans for infrastructure fund; will focus on scaling existing businesses.
items.quote: Right now, there are no plans for that. First, let us scale up the businesses that we have started up.

items.statement: SIP balances similar to last year with no growth from March to September; customers holding and buying as before.
items.quote: So, there is no growth from March to September in SIPs, but the balances are more or less same.

items.statement: Redemptions slightly higher currently.
items.quote: So we see the net figures only. So right now the redemptions are slightly higher. Yes, they are slightly higher.

items.statement: Small and mid-cap contribution to net flows grew to 43% this quarter versus previous quarter.
items.quote: Even if you look at it on a quarter-on-quarter basis, mid-cap and small-cap has grown to 43% in this quarter vis-a-vis the previous quarter.

items.statement: Redemptions more elevated in categories like BAF and MAF on hybrid side.
items.quote: Insofar as the redemption, we've also seen the redemption has been more elevated in the categories like BAF and MAF on the hybrid side. So that has also reflected in the net sales.

items.statement: Small-cap fund completely opened up; mid-cap slowly opening up; currently recommending large cap.
items.quote: Small caps, we see the opportunity. So, small-cap fund we have completely opened up. And at some point of time, when we have the call, we'll go and ask the investors to put money in small cap and get money in small cap. Mid cap, we are slowly opening up on the mid -cap side.

items.statement: Advisory AUM declining due to international outflows; new funds being launched in various geographies.
items.quote: And since last 1.5 years, we have had outflows in that. And that we have to manage the outflows right now. So, we are launching new funds in various geographies, and we are in regular touch with our existing distribution partners internationally.

items.statement: SIF is part of mutual fund business; margins and economics very similar to mutual funds.
items.quote: So we'll build this category and we are bullish on this category. But the margins and everything will be very similar to the way we manage mutual funds.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR30 per share declared by Board of Directors.
items.quote: Additionally, the Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of INR30 per share.

items.statement: Expects operational leverage to continue and a slightly upward margin trajectory through the rest of the year.
items.quote: From a margin trajectory perspective, what we expect is we expect operational leverage to continue playing out through rest of the year. While obviously there will be associated costs increase with revenue increases, we do see a slightly upward margin trajectory that should be playing out in rest of the year.

items.statement: Hopes H2 will be better than H1 in all businesses except Europe automotive.
items.quote: Overall, I would say yes, the only worry still seems to be the slowness in Europe from the automotive perspective, but other than that, I hope that in all other businesses H2 will be better than H1 for us.

items.statement: Confident of continuing growth in US and Asia; Europe remains wait and watch.
items.quote: We are pretty confident to continue the growth in US and in Asia piece, right? We would definitely continue to see sort of sustained growth there because we've won some large deals and ramp-ups are happening and we're hopeful that the adjacency piece will also pick up.

items.statement: Media and communication and healthcare expected to grow; transportation depends on Europe and US/India.
items.quote: But the other businesses, media and communication and the healthcare businesses, we based on the deals that we have signed and so on, we are pretty confident that H2 is going to be better than H1.

items.statement: Expects gradual margin improvement over next 2-3 quarters; no number given.
items.quote: So this is a work in progress, but yes, we will have to progressively move towards, over the next, I would say, 2 to 3 quarters, we will see that gradual improvement in our margins, right? We don't want to give a number at this point in time, but yes, we are working on it to see how where we can reach at the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Q3 typically short with fewer working days; awaiting customer direction on possible furloughs.
items.quote: Having said that, Q3 is typically a short quarter with fewer working days. While we await customer-specific direction on possible furloughs, we remain focused on sustaining growth in the second half while continuing to invest in our differentiated AI-first offerings and driving operational excellence.

items.statement: Utilization at 78%, up from last quarter, with room to improve.
items.quote: Utilization is about 78%. So we have sort of moved up from the last quarter. There's still possibly some room to grow.

items.statement: Peaked at around 81-82% utilization historically, still headroom.
items.quote: I think we peaked at around 81%, 82% utilization.

items.statement: Deal ramp-up typically takes two to three quarters to reach full level.
items.quote: Usually the deal ramp-up takes a couple of quarters, three quarters or so, to reach the full level.

items.statement: Large aerospace/defense deals will take at least two to three quarters to ramp up.
items.quote: No, it will take at least two to three quarters is what I would say. It's not an immediate ramp-up.

items.statement: Europe automotive decision-making delayed; deals in final shortlist not signed, timing uncertain.
items.quote: Unfortunately, because of the situation with the OEMs there, especially the big OEMs, we are seeing a delay in decision-making. We are there in the final shortlist in many of the deals there. But however, these deals have not been signed, and it is still a wait and watch in terms of when those decisions will be taken and so on.

items.statement: JLR going through challenges including layoffs; monitoring closely in H2.
items.quote: And we know JLR is going through its own challenges in terms of their own business performance and layoffs and so on. So we are watching that pretty closely and we will get to know about it, maybe across H2.

items.statement: Onsite-offshore revenue mix roughly 25:75, considered a good band.
items.quote: In terms of revenues, it's roughly about 25:75 that we have been running with for many quarters now, and I think that's a good place to be in.

items.statement: No guidance provided as a policy; no revision to guidance.
items.quote: As a policy, and in general, we don't provide guidance at all. So therefore there is no guidance, so therefore there is no revision to guidance.

items.statement: AI budgets continue to take from discretionary budgets but becoming more ROI-based.
items.quote: I think that continues because I think enterprises are committing AI budgets meant for enterprise transformation, not necessarily only for R&D, right? And to that extent, that does take away from what could otherwise be discretionary budgets.

items.statement: Others segment grew about 60-70% year-on-year but is only about 2% of revenue.
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, you'll see, I think, about a 75% growth in that piece. On one hand, it's just about 2%. But if you look at it on a year-on-year basis, you'll find that it's grown 60%, 70%, right?

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 98 bps sequentially to 5.6% in Q2 FY27; management aims to keep growing margins through operating leverage and price hikes
items.quote: margin improved by 98 basis points sequentially over Q1 of this financial year, reflecting a recovery in operating performance amid sustained cost pressures.

items.statement: Weighted average net price increase of 8% in Q2 FY27 (milk 6%, VAP 9-10%) against 11% YoY procurement cost inflation; September hikes higher, benefit accrues in Q3
items.quote: Overall NR increase for milk and value -added products is about 8%. So milk is about 6% and others is about 9% to 10%. Overall, 8% increase is there.

items.statement: Procurement prices rose slightly in October vs September; management hopes for cooling post-Diwali with buffalo flush but expects Q3 YoY inflation to continue around 11%
items.quote: But at this point in time, what we see is a slight increase of procurement prices in October compared to September as well.

items.statement: Milk procurement volumes grew 7% YoY to 17.28 lakh liters/day in Q2 despite monsoon constraints; milk sales volumes up 2% YoY to 12.35 lakh liters/day
items.quote: During Q2, milk procurement volumes increased 7% year -on-year to 17.28 lakh liters per day

items.statement: VAP revenue (excl. ghee/butter) grew 32% YoY to INR 4,510 mn in Q2; VAP contribution rose to 35.4% of revenue from 31.3% YoY; broad-based growth across lassi, buttermilk, ice cream, paneer, curd
items.quote: Value -added products remain a key growth engine with revenue, excluding ghee and butter, increasing 32% year -on-year to INR4,510 million in Q2

items.statement: Nourish+ high-protein paneer now >15% of paneer portfolio; daily curd sales crossed 500 tonnes; quarterly yogurt volumes exceeded 100 tonnes
items.quote: Nourish+ high -protein paneer accounting for more than 15% of our paneer portfolio.

items.statement: Newly commissioned ice cream facility adds capacity for Alpenvie and Get-A-Way; Heritage supplies 3,272 liters/day to Get-A-Way (71% stake)
items.quote: The newly commissioned ice cream facility provides additional manufacturing capacity for Alpenvie and Get -A-Way, supporting capacity absorption, operating leverage and future growth.

items.statement: Ice cream revenue target INR 500 cr in 6-7 years (excl. Get-A-Way); current run-rate ~INR 170-180 cr annualized vs INR 110 cr last year
items.quote: when we commissioned the ice cream factory, we said our vision is in the next 6 or 7 years, we want to get to INR500 crores of revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded from 4.6% in Q1 to 5.6% in Q2; employee, operating and freight costs fell as % of revenue; only raw material cost % rose
items.quote: we have moved from 4.6% to 5.6%. Our effort is to keep on growing, right? So our ability to absorb the costs are better.

items.statement: Milk procurement inflation remains elevated (11% YoY in Q2) due to El Niño, feed/fodder costs, uneven monsoon; management on wait-and-watch for flush season post-Diwali
items.quote: Our average landed milk procurement cost increased 11% year -on-year to INR 47.73 per liter in quarter 2, driven by sustained demand, limited improvement in milk arrivals and higher feed and fodder costs.

items.statement: Heritage Nutrivet (animal nutrition) revenue grew 47% YoY to INR 853 mn in Q2 with PBT of INR 37 mn; H1 revenue up 42% to INR 1,581 mn
items.quote: Heritage Nutrivet continued to deliver strong growth. The wholly owned subsidiary reported revenue of INR 853 million in quarter 2, an increase of 47% year -on-year with profit before tax of INR37 million.

items.statement: Cooperatives Aavin (TN) and Nandini (Karnataka) raised farmgate prices sharply; Heritage expects sales-side upside in Bangalore from Nandini hike effective Nov 1
items.quote: Aavin increasing milk procurement from up to INR38 to INR41 first and then INR41 to INR44. So that's about INR 6 per liter kind of increase.

items.statement: Cow milk procurement inflation outpacing buffalo milk despite higher cow milk supply, due to industry shift toward cheaper cow milk solids and cooperative hikes in cow milk belts
items.quote: cow milk actually, the total solids level price is almost getting closer to buffalo milk.

items.statement: New large conglomerate entry in dairy seen as category expansion opportunity; organized dairy only INR 4.5-5.5 lakh cr of INR 13-14 lakh cr market; Heritage growing 14-15% CAGR without geographic expansion
items.quote: There's humongous headroom for everyone to grow.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of ACT Group's cable TV business on September 15, 2026 for INR35.55 crores, adding ~6 lakh digital TV subscribers across four states
items.quote: We successfully completed the acquisition of cable television business of seven companies belonging to the ACT Group on September 15, 2026, for an aggregate cash consideration of INR35.55 crores.

items.statement: Acquiring remaining 74% stake in DL GTPL Cabnet for INR83.25 million, adding 1.5 lakh CATV subscribers in Gujarat, Maharashtra and MP
items.quote: Yes. So, this is the company where GTPL has 26% stake and we are going to purchase 74% stake at the said price. This company has 1.5 lakh subscriber base of CATV subscriber base, which is in the Gujarat, Maharashtra and a bit in MP.

items.statement: Digital cable TV subscriber base reached 11 million as of September 30, 2026, with 1.5 million additions in Q2 FY27, of which 10.30 million were paying subscribers
items.quote: our digital cable TV subscriber base as of September 30, 2026, stood at 11 million, addition of 1.5 million in this quarter, of which 10.30 million were paying

items.statement: Expect net additions of 1.8-1.9 million digital TV subscribers for full FY27, targeting 13-14 million CATV subscribers in 3 years with 7-8% annual growth
items.quote: And we are looking forward that by the end of the year, we will be somewhere around net additions of 1.8 million to 1.9 million subscriber base this year.

items.statement: Targeting broadband subscriber base of 1.2 million in next 3 years from current 1.07 million, with conversion rate improving from 17-18% to 20% of home pass
items.quote: And we are more than 1 million in broadband business, so we're looking forward that we can have somewhere in next 3 years, somewhere we are going to be close to 12 million subscriber base in 1.2 million subscriber base in the broadband side.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin at 20% in Q2 FY27, expected to improve by 150-250 bps by end of FY27 as acquisition synergies and HITS benefits materialize
items.quote: In H1 FY27, we have 21% the operational EBITDA, which we expect to increase by 150 basis points to 250 basis points once we fully realize all the synergy benefits and the delivery cost benefits due to HITS implementation and this.

items.statement: ACT acquisition currently at 12% operating EBITDA margin, expected to reach 25-26% after full integration into GTPL systems and environment
items.quote: Already the revenues are reported there in our the ACT revenue. And somew here the EBITDA margin right now is operating margin if you talk about, is 12%, which we are looking forward that it should start giving us somewhere around 25% margin, 25% to 26% margin

items.statement: No additional capex or opex required for current 436 GB monthly data consumption per broadband user; capacity can scale with only 10% incremental investment if usage doubles
items.quote: No, for this consumption and there's no additional capex or opex, I'll say, because we have the technology in such a way that it can be flexible. So, right now, at this consumption level, we have not did any capex and opex.

items.statement: Broadband ARPU increased to INR470 in Q2 FY27 driven by existing subscribers migrating to higher plans; active broadband subscribers at 1.07 million with 10,000 Q-o-Q additions
items.quote: Broadband ARPU for Q2 FY27 stood at INR470, while average monthly data consumption per user was 436 GB.

items.statement: Broadband ARPU growth of INR5 year-on-year driven by subscriber adoption of higher plans, not price hikes; management sees further ARPU upside from plan upgrades without affecting retention
items.quote: Yes, so this is because the subscribers are adopting to the higher plans, the current subscriber who were at the lower plans, they are adopting to the higher plans, and that is moving our ARPU up.

items.statement: PAT negative INR50 lakh in Q2 FY27 due to INR75 million impact from INR45 million forex loss and INR30 million amortization from seven new transponders; these are notional costs expected to improve over time
items.quote: The consolidated PAT stands negative INR50 lakh in this quarter due to additional impact of INR75 million, which is INR45 million on account of forex loss and INR30 million amortization impact due to seven new transponders, which is in standalone financials.

items.statement: GTPL Infinity HITS platform launched November 2025; >60% of existing network migrated, targeting full migration by December 2026-January 2027 to unlock delivery cost savings
items.quote: Already, more than 60% has happened. The existing network has gone in to the HITS platform. We are looking forward that by December or maximum by January, all the existing network will convert into HITS platform, and we will start getting the whole delivery cost benefits in our books.

items.statement: Broadband home pass reached 6 million as of September 30, 2026; conversion rate improved from 13-14% to 17-18%, targeting 20% with new TrueFiber branding and aggressive market strategy
items.quote: Our active subscriber base stood at 1.07 million at the end of quarter, which is 10,000 additions Q-o-Q, while broadband home pass reached 6 million as of September 30, 2026.

items.statement: Expect double-digit subscription revenue growth in both digital TV and broadband, with operational EBITDA margin improvement of 150-250 bps in FY27 as synergies and HITS benefits fully realize
items.quote: We are looking forward that we are going to have a double-digit growth in subscription revenues in both the businesses and improving our operational EBITDA in comparison to last financial year.

items.statement: Digital TV market becoming more challenging with technology changes and delivery medium shifts; company gearing up to offer complementary broadband and entertainment products to retain customers
items.quote: Next year, as you know, the market is becoming more and more challenging with the change of the technologies, change of the delivery mediums and everything.

items.statement: Appointed new broadband CEO Vivek Raina three months ago; completed full network migration to GPON/FTTH; targeting return to 20,000+ monthly broadband additions
items.quote: And yes, I would like the network is completely migrated into the GPON side. So, the basically the now the entire network, you can say, it's a completely FTTH market.

items.statement: Retail Health loss ratio comfortable range 65-70%.

items.statement: Motor sales expected to continue surpassing previous trends.

items.statement: Growth may moderate due to higher base.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle mix maintained within 20-25% band.

items.statement: Industry Motor combined ratio at 131% not workable.

items.statement: Retention improved by 3-5% across retail lines.

items.statement: EV share of motor book at 7-8%.

items.statement: Banca business contribution 12.5-15% of total premium.

items.statement: EOM maintained within 30%.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining medium- to long-term EBITDA margins within guided range of 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Expects sustainable EPC margins in high single-digit range over medium to long term.

items.statement: FMEG EBITDA margin target of 8% to 10% for FY30.
items.quote: So over the longer term, I believe we would end up in that kind of a range of 8% to 10% of the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: EHV plant commissioning expected in FY28.
items.quote: So I would like to take this opportunity to sort of also let the investor community know that in terms of our EHV plant timelines, we are expecting the EHV plant to now commission somewhere in FY 2028, the next year, though, so FY28.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to trend towards long-term operating range of 45 to 50 days.
items.quote: As these benefits gradually normalize, we expect the working capital cycle to trend towards our long-term operating range of 45 to 50 days.

items.statement: Second half demand looks promising with healthy growth expected.
items.quote: Second half also looks very promising, and it's largely driven through the kind of demand that we're seeing right now. We are seeing healthy growth in the second half as well.

items.statement: EPC order book is close to INR9,000 crores to INR10,000 crores.
items.quote: Roughly the order book, I would say it is close to around INR9,000 crores, INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: Passes on copper price changes to customers: monthly for cables, fortnightly for wires.
items.quote: And usually what will happen is that we will pass it on to the end customer. For cables, we do it in a month, and for wires, we do it every fortnight.

items.statement: Confident exports will pick up due to strong order book pipeline.
items.quote: So we are very happy with the kind of growth that we are seeing in exports, and we are very much confident that with the kind of order book pipeline that we are having, exports is certainly going to pick up from here.

items.statement: Wires outpaced cables in H1, but no guidance on future mix.
items.quote: Today in the first half, definitely wires have done better than cables, but there's a lot of play around it. So I think we can't give you on record that on the kind of growth any segment that we see.

items.statement: No adverse material impact expected from Asier Metals proceedings.

items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, our unexecuted order book stood at 7,237 crore, up by 32% year-on-year, providing strong revenue visibility over the medium term. The order book is executable over the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Order inflows of Rs 1,169 crore in Q2 FY27, 97% YoY growth
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, we received order inflows of 1,169 crores, 97% year-on-year growth over low base of last year this time.

items.statement: Confident of achieving FY27 guidance of 25% revenue growth and 9-10% PAT margin
items.quote: Following our Q2 performance, we remain confident of achieving FY27 guidance and continue to remain on track with our growth plans for the full year.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 forecast of 25% growth and 9-10% PAT margin
items.quote: So, our target is to reach a growth of 25% and beyond. So, we are keeping it the same.

items.statement: Changodar expansion near completion, commercial production expected around Diwali, capex ~Rs 150 crore, adds 35,000 MVA capacity
items.quote: Our ongoing transformer manufacturing expansion at Changodar is near completion, with the commercial production expected to commence around Diwali. The additional capacity will further strengthen our capability to execute our growing order book and support the next phase of the revenue growth.

items.statement: Backward integration projects progressing; CTC plant commissioning by Diwali, commercial production Q4 FY27; pressboard plant to add 30% capacity at Moraiya
items.quote: Backward integration projects are progressing as per timeline.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.1% vs 8.8% YoY and 13.3% QoQ; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.6% vs 13.4% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 16.1% compared to 8.8% in Q2FY26 and 13.3% in Q1 FY27. This reflects the benefit of higher operating leverage and improved utilization level during the quarter.

items.statement: Backward integration expected to add 200-300 bps margin expansion, full effect by FY29
items.quote: So, we are looking at around 200 basis point to 300 basis point margin expansion through this backward integration.

items.statement: Supportive demand environment across power generation, transmission, renewables, data centers, railway electrification, EV infrastructure
items.quote: From an industry perspective, the underlying demand environment cont inues to remain supportive. India is witnessing a significant investment across power generation, transmission infrastructure, renewable energy integration and grid

items.statement: Order book 55-60% high voltage (400 kV+); Q2 execution ~56% power transformers
items.quote: Roughly we have around 55% of order which is having a high voltage class. 55% to 60% is a high voltage class, 400 kV and above.

items.statement: Working capital days target 110-120 days by end FY27 from current 154 days; positive free cash flow expected after working capital reduction
items.quote: It should be below 120 days. We are trying to, you know, reach at 120, and once we reach there, we would like to see close to between 110 days and 120 days this year.

items.statement: Established UK subsidiary in Sep 2026 to strengthen Europe presence; potential future manufacturing base
items.quote: In September 2026, we established a subsidiary in UK to strengthen our customer support and expand our presence in the UK and European markets.

items.statement: HVDC converter transformer qualification expected within 18 months; repair and testing ongoing
items.quote: So, we are also in the process of getting the converted transformers approved also. So, within next 18 months, we'll be fully be able to do the HVDC and converter transformers.

items.statement: USD 1 billion revenue target by late FY29 or early 2030 including backward integration product sales
items.quote: It will be late part of FY29 or early 2030.

items.statement: No additional capex or funding needed for USD 1 billion target; current QIP proceeds and internal accruals sufficient
items.quote: No. Because see, we are already doing this capacity expansion, backwar d integration projects, funding, etcetera, is already well planned. So, no additional capex

items.statement: Advertising revenue impact of ~INR40 crore shifted from Q2 to Q3 due to Navratri timing; optimistic on next two quarters despite geopolitical concerns
items.quote: we believe there is an impact of almost around INR40 crores. Now with that shifting into Q3 and the overall momentum, what we believe is there, though in certain parts of India, the monsoon is not playing well because in Rajasthan, even there's a rains happening even today.

items.statement: Endeavor to achieve high single-digit to early double-digit full-year advertising revenue growth
items.quote: That's what our endeavor is. Looking at this -- what we've seen in the last 7, 8 days of festival, overall momentum is good. let's hope this continues.

items.statement: Newsprint cost per tonne increased ~21% YoY from INR47,000 to INR57,000; expected to soften 2-3% in Q3/Q4
items.quote: What we were paying INR47,000 per tonne average cost, we are paying right now almost INR57,000. So there are almost 20.8% to be more precise 21% is the impact on the newsprint cost.

items.statement: No cover price hikes planned; increasing price would accelerate circulation decline
items.quote: We have taken this call, if you remember, a year back or so, that overall, let's face it, the re is a change on the number of copies. And furthermore, if we increase the cover price, that will further accelerate the decline. So we don't want to do that

items.statement: FMCG ad spend down 2% YoY in Q2 but underlying trend ~single-digit growth; real estate flat to single-digit; jewelry strong; BFSI/IPO up 50%; healthcare strong double-digit; auto flat; education single-digit
items.quote: If I look at this quarter, FMCG, the FMCG right now is at minus 2%. But as I mentioned, this quarter would be a wrong way to comparison. So I would say almost single -digit growth, even considering the festival in this quarter.

items.statement: Digital subscription price hike from INR149 to INR199 on experimental basis; early results decent; revenue impact too early to quantify
items.quote: First of all, the price hike, which we have taken from INR149 to INR199, this will all be experimental basis. It's not a flat. Some places we have even tried slightly lesser, even monthly price and all that.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 4-5 quarters; production equipment in place
items.quote: we don't have any large capex planned because all the machines, production e quipments and all are all in place. So we don't see -- foresee any major capex coming in a couple of quarters or maybe 4, 5 quarters ahead

items.statement: Cash and bank balance ~INR1,120 crores; INR5/share interim dividend paid in Q1; further distribution to be decided by Board
items.quote: As on today, company has a total cash and bank balance of around INR1,120 crores. And as you know, the company has already paid INR5 per share as the first interim dividend in the Q1.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and monsoon irregularities cited as key risks to advertising momentum in H2
items.quote: I don't know how the overall 3 or next 6 months are going to pan out. Especially I'm more concerned about the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Expecting high teens revenue growth for FY27 and aspiring for double-digit growth over the long term
items.quote: Over the long term, we want to aspire for a double-digit growth. And yes, for the year, we are expecting a high teens, and that's what we've just said.

items.statement: Planning a 5% consumer price increase in Q3 FY27 split between 2-3% frontal price hike and similar ml-age reduction
items.quote: We will now follow it up with another round of price increase and ml-age reduction in quarter 3. In this round, we are approximately taking a 5% increase in consumer price, which will be split roughly equally between frontal price increase of 2% to 3% and a similar contribution coming through ml-age reductions.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin at 59.9%, H1 at 60.8%; EBITDA margin 25%, PAT margin 21% despite raw material volatility
items.quote: Our gross margins for the quarter were at 59.9%, and overall for the first half of the year at 60.8%. Despite the sequential reduction in gross margin, our teams have been able to rally around and deliver very strong savings in fixed costs and employee costs, which have allowed us to deliver a near-term high EBITDA margin of 25% and a PAT margin of 21%.

items.statement: Almond Drops Hair Oil delivered double-digit unit volume growth across pack groups and channels, led by small and medium packs
items.quote: Almond Drops Hair Oil continues with its strong performance in this quarter and has delivered double -digit unit volume growth. This growth came across pack groups and sales channels. And while all pack groups have done well, the growth was particularly led by small and medium-sized packs, which outperformed the overall brand.

items.statement: Growth portfolio brands relaunched with refined propositions in amla oils, body lotion, and Banjara's extensions; profitability substantially improved
items.quote: In amla oils, we have refined the consumer proposition and are testing the new mix in general trade. In body lotion, we have upgraded both the product and packaging, and will test it on e-commerce. In Banjara's, we have introduced packs that extend the brand into large adjacent categories, which could offer significant growth potential for us if we are successful.

items.statement: Cost environment remains volatile due to West Asia war and edible oil inflation; committed to calibrated pricing actions to protect P&L while being fair to consumers
items.quote: Going forward, the cost environment remains volatile, and we stand committed to taking actions as appropriate to protect our P&L while being fair to our consumers.

items.statement: International business grew ahead of company average in H1 FY27 except Bangladesh; sharp improvement in international EBITDA margins on revenue scale-up and cost optimization
items.quote: channel for the full H1 has grown ahead of the company growth, and except for Bangladesh, most of our other ke y markets individually have also grown ahead of the company average. Bangladesh is witnessing a tough operating environment and grew in the teens. Our international business is also improving a sharp improvement in profitability. And on the back of revenue scale -up, margin correction, an

items.statement: Maintain 30%-35% AUM CAGR and 35%-40% profitability CAGR on a 12-month forward basis
items.quote: Guidance, we will maintain 30% to 35% CAGR from the AUM perspective, and 35%-40% CAGR from profitability perspective.

items.statement: Target INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM in 2-3 years with 30%-35% YoY growth
items.quote: We believe that the current supply chain mandates we have from our anchor clients, we can achieve this AUM growth in next 2 to 3 years, which will translate into 30%-35% AUM growth Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Expect INR7,000 crore AUM by FY27 year-end
items.quote: today when we have book of INR5,700 crores and looking at the current run rate, probably we may end up achieving INR7,000 crores kind of AUM by year end

items.statement: Invested INR48 crore for 15% stake in tech subsidiary to build in-house AI digital stack
items.quote: the board has approved an investment of approximately INR48 crores to set up a finance company in the GIFT City

items.statement: Added 14 new anchor corporates in H1; targeting 2 new anchors per month for next 12-18 months
items.quote: in H1 like we have acquired 14 new anchor corporates. So how many additional new anchors do we expect to onboard in the second half? Vinay Gupta: The target in our mind is 2 anchors per month

items.statement: Maintain ROA >4.5%, cost-to-income <15%, yield ~13% (11-15% range)
items.quote: We have also achieved all our key operating parameters: maintained nil NPA, return on assets is more than 4.5% and cost-to-income continues to remain less than 15% and we plan to maintain this in quarters to come as well.

items.statement: Supply chain 70% of AUM (group ecosystem down to 25%); 60+ anchor brands; steel 35%, auto 20%
items.quote: We continue to be a supply -chain-focused NBFC, supply cha in contributing to ~70% of our AUM today. This is despite reduction in our dependency on the group ’s ecosystem . The contribution of group’s ecosystem to our book has come down to 25% now. Currently, we are powering the ecosystem of more than 60 brands in the country

items.statement: No equity raise this year; board approved leverage increase to 4x debt-to-equity; AIF application filed with SEBI
items.quote: No. Our mid-term target was to not leverage ourselves beyond debt-to-equity of 3x. But now considering the growth which has front-loaded, we are revising our leverage to debt-to-equity of 4x. Today in our board meeting also, board has approved the incremental borrowing, so we would like to leverage ourselves more.

items.statement: GIFT City subsidiary for overseas supply chain; operational in ~1 year; dual RBI/IFSCA approval
items.quote: For that reason, we are setting up our wholly owned subsidiary in GIFT City. But it has a dual approval requirement from RBI and IFSCA, so it's a long gestation. This is going to take maybe a year or so to be operational there.

items.statement: AIF Cat III equity fund filed with SEBI; fee-based AMC model; no own capital deployment; launch timeline uncertain
items.quote: We have filed the application to SEBI. We are waiting for the approval. Once the approva l is there, we will launch it. As the thing stand today, we have incorporated the company, filed the application, waiting for the SEBI approval

items.statement: RBI draft revolving credit guidelines aligned with current term-based model; only minor doc/system tweaks needed
items.quote: RBI guidelines currently are in draft form. Whatever discussions we have had directly, or indirectly with RBI, we submitted our presentation also, I believe the intention of regulator is that NBFCs should only do term-based business, and supply chain by nature is a term-based business. We are not allowing extension, or rollover of any of our facilities.

items.statement: Focus remains on delivering sustainable VNB growth, balancing growth, profitability, risk and prudence; protection and annuity stay central.
items.quote: Our strategy remains unchanged, delivering sustainable VNB growth while balancing business growth, profitability, and risk and prudence. Protection and annuity stay central to our strategy, addressing significant underpenetrated needs in India.

items.statement: Retail protection growth expected to taper in H2 from 40-50% levels to more moderate levels.
items.quote: The expectation is that as you get into H2 of this year, those growth numbers should taper down from the 40%-50% that we've been seeing to more moderate levels.

items.statement: Par to non-par mix in last quarter broadly in the range of 60:40.
items.quote: So this year, for instance, has started to move towards non-par, and specifically in the last quarter, the mix is broadly in the range of 60:40, par to non-par.

items.statement: VNB margin expansion from FY2026 to H1 FY2027 largely explained by product mix shift.
items.quote: The right way to look at is from financial year 2026 numbers, which we closed the year at a margin of 24.7% and we closed H1 this year at 26%. As we had discussed at the Q1 call itself, a large portion of this movement fundamentally is the product mix and that continues from quarter one all the way to quarter two as well.

items.statement: Company repriced non-par products as a continuous exercise based on market yields.
items.quote: So we have repriced. This is a continuous exercise for us. We look at what are the yields that are available in market, and then we offer that to customers. It is a continuous process, Shreya.

items.statement: Improved profitability from yields and opex is passed on to customers via better pricing to propel demand.
items.quote: The idea is to be able to pass on to the customer, because clearly you should be able to create demand. If your product is a rupee cheaper than the next competitor, then it clearly helps propel that demand.

items.statement: If rates stay high longer, non-par and annuity can become a larger proportion of business.
items.quote: If the rates stay high for longer, then it is likely that non-par as a share, and this also adds annuity to it, both of these can become a larger proportion of the business, not just for us, for others as well.

items.statement: Annuity and guaranteed products attractive in IRRs and have done well across all distribution channels.
items.quote: These products are very attractive in terms of IRRs, both the annuities, which have been on the regular pay variety, as well as the guaranteed products, which also are both income as well as lump sum variety. And they've done quite well across all of our distribution channels.

items.statement: Consultation paper on distribution economics is early; regulator collecting feedback, no closure yet.
items.quote: I think it's a consultation paper at this point. It's not a draft regulation. The regulator has set a time towards the end of this month to collect feedback from all stakeholders, including the general public, with the objective that it is customer-centric and it is policyholder at its core.

items.statement: Too early to call volume impact from proposed commission structure changes; renewal commission space provides comfort.
items.quote: It's too difficult to call, Swarnabha. The way you also look at this is that there is sufficient space that the regulator has set out in terms of renewal commission.

items.statement: Operating expenses excluding GST and stamp duty reduced at 8% CAGR over last three years.
items.quote: Our operating expenses, excluding GST and stamp duty, have reduced at a CAGR of 8% over the last three years, an absolute 22% reduction in FY2026 compared to FY2023, which reflects the steady and deliberate progress that we have made.

items.statement: Company comfortable with IFRS and RBC numbers; strategy unchanged under new standards.
items.quote: We're comfortable with the way that the IFRS numbers are stacking up. We're comfortable with RBC.

items.statement: Agency channel to continue receiving investment; gross agent additions grew 23% in half-year.
items.quote: I think the opex advantage that we have allows us to continue to invest in Agency. And even when you look at this half-year, in terms of the gross addition of agents, that's 23% growth, which is ahead of the rest of the market.

items.statement: Company does not provide growth guidance; focus on medium-term sustainable growth.
items.quote: Again, we don't provide guidance. We can give you what we should look at from the medium term.

items.statement: October trends too early to call, only 10-12 days into the quarter.
items.quote: October too early to call. It's just been about 10-12 days, too early in the quarter to call this out.

items.statement: Credit life growth in line with protection growth; wide diversity of partners including parent bank.
items.quote: So the growth in credit life has been quite in line with what you're seeing in the protection growth for this quarter as well. So, it's a fairly decent growth that we're seeing at this point.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 ESOP non-cash expense expected around INR79-80 crores.
items.quote: Yes. So the noncash expense for ESOP cost for the full year FY '27 would be around INR79 crores, INR80 crores.

items.statement: AIF fees are 80-90 bps, above mutual fund equity book; discretionary PMS similar to equity MF; non-discretionary PMS strategic; government mandates highly contested.
items.quote: On the margins question, AIF is a margin-accretive business. Fees here sit above what we earn on our mutual fund equity book in the range of 80 to 90 basis points depending on the product.

items.statement: SIF product launches expected over next couple of quarters.
items.quote: We are now well set, and you will see a couple of product launches in this space over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Costs split into inflation-linked routine expenses and upfront investments in people, technology, distribution.
items.quote: So I mentioned, I think it's split into two. One is like the regular , the operating expenses that should be like inflation linked as the business grows and in line with the gr owth in the business in terms of size and broadly speaking, these are like routine costs that we continuously monitor and manage.

items.statement: Alternative investment team has over 20 professionals, expanding investor servicing, operations, sales, distribution.
items.quote: So between alternative and PMS, when I say alternative, both private equity and private credit, we've got more than 20 investment professionals now and significantly expanding our capacity on investor servicing, on operations, on the whole sales and then the distribution side, so on and so forth.

items.statement: Mutual fund investment team grew from 30 to nearly 40 professionals and will continue to grow.
items.quote: But even on the mutual fund side, team till a couple of years back was like 30 professionals. Now number is like closer to 40, and this will continue to grow.

items.statement: Investing upfront in international business despite small AUM due to potential.
items.quote: Same thing is on the international side, where the AUM is not very large, but we are investing upfront because we see a lot of potential in that business.

items.statement: Investing in AI-led capabilities across major business functions with upfront costs and future benefits.
items.quote: And then, of course, the technology where a team of engineers working on AI-led capabilities across major business functions. So this is like upfront investments, but in terms of the cost saving, potential cost saving or the potential higher revenues will occur over a period of time.

items.statement: Board distributed almost all post-tax cash profits as dividend; balance sheet used for seed capital in alternate platforms.
items.quote: For the last year, the Board ha s declared a dividend, which effectively where we have distributed the almost entire post-tax cash profits that we generate. The balance sheet that we have, currently, we are using for seed capital for all our alternate platforms.

items.statement: Seeding new strategies requires ongoing seed capital.
items.quote: It is a continuing process. As we keep seeding new strategies, this will require seed capital.

items.statement: H1 cost skewed by CSR expenses in Q1; request to look at full-year expenses.
items.quote: Sir, actually, we had mentioned this in our last quarterly call. There were some CSR expenses which were taken up in the first quarter. And because of that, you are seeing the H1 numbers getting kind of a bit skewed.

items.statement: SIP market share increased when excluding STP; systematic transactions rose from 17 million in June to nearly 19 million in September.
items.quote: If you strip out STP and look at SIP alone, our market share has actually gone up. I repeat. If you strip out STP and look at only the SIP, our market share has actually gone up.

items.statement: Monthly systematic transaction book grew nearly 5x in 5 years to around INR48 billion; industry grew 3x.
items.quote: And if we step back for a moment, monthly systematic transaction book has grown nearly 5x in about 5 years to around INR48 billion and industry in the same p eriod would have grown 3x.

items.statement: Small cap fund remains 0.5% of small-cap universe market cap, same as June 2019.
items.quote: So if you look at, for example, the small cap fund and some of the people have heard saying that now it's INR40,000 crores. But it was 0.5% of the small-cap universe market cap in June '19, if I remember correctly. And it's still like 0.5% of the market cap universe today.

items.statement: Weighted average market cap of mid and small cap funds below category average.
items.quote: And also the other thing that we constantly look at both for our mid-cap fund and small-cap fund is the weighted average market cap of that fund vis-a-vis the benchmark and vis -a-vis the category average. And our weighted average market cap in that sits below the category average.

items.statement: Launched two outbound funds in GIFT City; six inbound funds; will keep evaluating product bouquet.
items.quote: Yes, so continuously been expanding the product bouquet. We have got six funds for inbound investment that is investment by global investors in India. And recently, we have launched two products for outbound where there's an opportunity for Indian investors to invest globally.

items.statement: Targets $600-650 million UBS flow exchange by March end, with $300-325 million already done.
items.quote: I think onboarding has got initiated. So, in some senses, we've internally looked at a target of exchanging $600 odd million in flows for the current financial year.

items.statement: Expects 100-150 bps cost-to-income improvement year-on-year.
items.quote: I think we had guided for a 1 - 1.5% kind of overall improvement year-on-year. I think we are well on course to achieve that.

items.statement: Aims to move cost-to-income from 48 towards 46-47 over 12-18 months.
items.quote: I think we'll continue our journey and keep it going over the next 12 - 18 months. Doesn't necessarily mean our standalone employee cost numbers will reduce, but we will continue to try and make the firm as productive as possible.

items.statement: Targets doubling profits over 3.5 years, no need to raise capital, aiming for 20% ROE.
items.quote: I think our first target really in that sense will be to ensure that over the next 2.5 - 3 odd years or rather 3.5 years we are able to double our profits. If we can double our profits over the next 3.5 years and, honestly, don’t see any need to raise capital. We can ensure that we hit the 20% number.

items.statement: Expects to be full-fledged capital markets platform by March 31, with big pickup in Q1 next financial year.
items.quote: I think from a full stack perspective we’ll be really ready on 31st March, first week of April, in terms of the entire team and talent being there. Needless to say, early green shoots in terms of us winning the right set of mandates has always been on the cards.

items.statement: Expects equity brokerage to grow from ₹8-9 crores to ₹15-20 crores per month.
items.quote: I think if you just look at our current ultra HNI, HNI clients, we should be doing around about ₹15 - 20 crores a month. And that’s more or less business which should be captive within us because we’ve already got the clients with us and all their accounts are with us.

items.statement: Expects TBR to grow to ₹800-1,000 crores when revenue reaches ₹5,000-5,500 crores.
items.quote: I think, if I just fast-forward my year, the day we are doing around about ₹5,000-₹5,200 crores of revenue or ₹5,500 crores of revenue, I see the TBR being in the ZIP code of ₹800-₹1,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects 40-50 bps retention on UBS flows both ways.
items.quote: I think it’s safe to assume 40 - 50 basis points of retention would broadly come through.

items.statement: Expects ₹3,000-3,500 crores fund redemption over next 6-18 months, hopes most money returns.
items.quote: I think, yes, that fund will go back over the space of next 6 - 18 months. So, that’s the only large fund, I think, which is up for redemption, which is around about ₹3,000 - 3,500 crores.

items.statement: Expects cost-to-income ratio to stay within 100-200 bps as new hires are added.
items.quote: But overall, all three things put together, I think we should be able to kind of keep it within the 100 - 200 basis points cost to income ratio as we build it out.

items.statement: Expects asset management flows to meet targets for current year.
items.quote: I think flows will kind of come back and overall should be in a position to meet our targets for the current year.

items.statement: Expects HNI business to break even on direct costs soon.
items.quote: With productivity improving and a growing feeder pipeline into UHNI, we expect the business to break even on direct costs soon.

items.statement: Expects 18-20% ROE over 3-3.5 years on tangible net worth.
items.quote: I think we definitely would aim to, over a period of 3 - 3.5 years, ensure that we are around that 20% zip code on the tangible net worth.

items.statement: Expects 50% of flows from wallet share and 50% from new mandates going forward.
items.quote: I think if we can reach this number, it is true it is just one quarter, but I think if we can reach the number where we are able to go 50/50 with our clients, I think that will give a fair degree of confidence for us to keep achieving our net flow targets.

items.statement: Expects 1:2 split of net flows from new clients and existing clients.
items.quote: I think largely we look at 1:2 split, 1/3 rd from new clients and 2/3rd from existing clients.

items.statement: Expects 65-72-73 bps overall retention on large mandates.
items.quote: But I think if I look at the relationship, overall, I think we are coming back to the same 65 - 72 - 73 basis points overall.

items.statement: Stand-alone operating margin guidance of around 45% on an annual basis, subsuming all expenses including IPL
items.quote: So this margin guidance of about 45% for the broking and distribution business on an annual basis, subsumes all the expenses, including the IPL.

items.statement: Consolidated operating margin guidance of 40% to 45% in the near term
items.quote: On a consol basis, so the guidance is anywhere between 40% to 45% in the near term.

items.statement: Stand-alone operating margin reached 48.9% in Q2 FY27, exceeding guided range of 40% to 45%
items.quote: At the stand-alone level, operating margins reached 48.9%, exceeding our guided range of 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Normalized consolidated operating margin stable at 43.8% in Q2 FY27 vs 43.6% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Importantly, after normalizing for seasonal IPL expenditure and ESOP-related reversals, consolidated operating margins remained stable at 43.8% compared to 43.6% in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance of about ₹1,100 crores including ESOP cost for FY27, flat year-on-year
items.quote: So we'll continue to maintain our guidance of about ₹ 1,100 crores of employee costs, including the cost of stock options for this financial year, which is flat for year-on-year comparison.

items.statement: Average client funding book reached lifetime high of ₹74.5 billion, up 40.5% year-on-year; closing book at record ₹82.1 billion
items.quote: The average client funding book increased over 40% year-on-year to ₹ 74.5 billion, while the closing book reached a record ₹ 82.1 billion.

items.statement: September average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 million, up nearly 12% from August; October industry F&O ADTO up ~39% month-to-date vs September
items.quote: In September, average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 million, up nearly 12% from August.

items.statement: Gross broking income now ~55% of total revenues vs ~60% a year ago; interest income grew 34% YoY to ₹5.1 billion; distribution income growing healthily
items.quote: Gross broking income now accounts for approximately 55% of total revenues compared with nearly 60% a year ago.

items.statement: Credit distribution annualized run rate reached ₹33 billion in September, highest ever; credit models upgraded and loan against securities beta launched
items.quote: In September, we delivered our highest ever credit distribution, taking our annualized run rate to ₹ 33 billion.

items.statement: Wealth management AUM at ₹160 billion, up 19.1% over Q1 FY27; evaluating comprehensive play in Asset Management including new leadership
items.quote: Our wealth business is gaining depth as well with Ionic Wealth AUM at ₹ 160 billion, up 19.1% over Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Received authorization as Global Access Provider in IFSC; piloting U.S. stocks on platform with external U.S. brokerage partner
items.quote: We have received authorization to operate as a Global Access Provider in the IFSC. With that, we are piloting U.S. stocks on our platform.

items.statement: MTF lending rate unchanged at 14.99%; cost of borrowing marginally up due to RBI rate hike but within tolerance, NIMs not impacted
items.quote: I think for the time being, we are not looking at any increase in the lending cost. So it remains at 14.99%.

items.statement: MTF book quality solid: 85%+ in blue chip and good categories; 84% of funded clients have exposure below ₹100,000; 82% of book less than 30 days old; delinquencies negligible
items.quote: Largely, our book is good and blue chip constitutes almost upwards of 85%.

items.statement: H2 FY27 performance expected to replicate H1 FY27 numbers.

items.statement: AUM will be better than last year.

items.statement: ROCE grew nearly 14% and ROTA near 5% in H1.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing excluding TREPS was 7.08% in Q2 FY27 versus 7.07% in Q1 FY27.

items.quote: On interest rate risk management, over 70% of our Assets Under Management are on floating rates, enabling interest rate adjustments to be seamlessly passed on to borrowers with minimal time lag.

items.quote: To drive profitable growth, we are actively pursuing high-margin segments, including small and medium businesses as well as exporters.

items.statement: Primary insurers recalibrated crop insurance exposure to align with seasonal and environmental factors, moderating sequential reinsurance volume.
items.quote: Primary insurance carriers recalibrated their exposure to crop insurance to align with seasonal and environmental factors, which moderated sequential volume.

items.statement: Jio Credit AUM mix: mortgages 44.5%, corporate and SME loans 44.2%, retail LAS 11.3%.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank received regulatory approvals to launch 3-in-1 Savings Account and act as Banker to the Issue for public offerings including IPOs.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also received key regulatory approvals to launch our 3-in-1 Savings Account as well as to act as ‘Banker to the Issue’ for public offerings, including IPOs, which will open up new revenue streams for the payments bank.

items.statement: Jio Allianz General Insurance is in advanced stages for regulatory approvals to commence operations.
items.quote: In general and health insurance, Jio Allianz General Insurance Limited is in advanced stages for securing regulatory approvals to commence operations.

items.statement: GIFT City entity received IFSCA approval to launch BlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund, planned for launch during the current quarter.

items.statement: JioBlackRock AMC partnered with over 15,000 mutual fund and SIF distributors and launched Regular Plans across all product offerings.
items.quote: As highlighted in our distribution strategy, we have now partnered with over 15,000 Mutual Fund and Specialized Investment Fund distributors, and have launched Regular Plans across all our product offerings to complement our Direct Plans.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 20-25% for the year, assuming flat gold prices.
items.quote: We will continue to give the same guidance in spite of the gold prices being almost flat. So we will give a AUM growth of about 20% to 25% for the year.

items.statement: Targeting 3% ROA and 18% ROE.
items.quote: Our target ROA we are trying to reach is 3% and correspondingly try and touch an 18% ROE.

items.statement: Credit cost to remain below 1%.
items.quote: This guidance that we have given is the credit cost that w e will manage will be way below 1%.

items.statement: GNPA to remain below 2%.
items.quote: If you remember last year as well as the start of the year, I told you that the GNPAs will also be below 2%.

items.statement: Plan to add at least 150 branches in H2 FY27.
items.quote: In addition to the 74 branches we added in quarter 2, we propose to add at least another 150 branches in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Expects better performance in H2 due to seasonality.
items.quote: Historically, the second half of the year is a much stronger period for us, which is giving us confidence that in spite of the headwinds you mentioned, we would be able to perform to our guidance, which we have been giving in the earlier quarters for this year on AUM growth.

items.statement: Small ticket LAP disbursals to be best in last 8-9 quarters in Q3.
items.quote: I can't give you a definite guidance, but I can tell you so much that it will be amongst the last 8 or 9 quarters, it will be the best quarter compared to the last 8 or 9 quarters.

items.statement: Yield trajectory to improve in Q3 for small ticket LAP.
items.quote: But you will definitely see a different yield trajectory i n Q3. Definitely, it will be more than Q2 as well as the disbursals will be more.

items.statement: Tonnage growth to improve in H2.
items.quote: So you will see a different trajectory in H2 for tonnage.

items.statement: Will use multiple levers to manage yields and ROA.
items.quote: As far as the yield is concerned, - for Q3 and Q4, we will use all levers possible, whether it is yield, whether it is LTV and growth, it will be a combination.

items.statement: Stage II and III increases are technical, not credit concerns.
items.quote: As far as the gold piece is concerned, this Stage II is technical in nature. You are aware, most of the gold loan product is a 3 -month or 2.5 -month behavioural tenor product. So this will not translate into a credit cost.

items.statement: Branch profitability at INR6-7 crores AUM in 12-13 months.
items.quote: Typically, a branch, if it reaches about INR6 crores to INR7 crores of AUM, it turns profitable for us. when the price is going on an upward trajectory or even the price that is there today, in 12 to 13 months, the branch starts touching that number.

items.statement: Approval rates for ST LAP improved to mid-40%.
items.quote: So approval rates for earlier when we were coming out of the woods had dropped down to about 30% levels. Now steadily, they have moved up to the mid-40% or the early 40% levels.

items.statement: Insurance income contribution to ROA is about 0.1%.
items.quote: So, from an ROA tree perspective, I would put the number at about 0.1% in the ROA tree from an income perspective, a little over 0.1%.

items.statement: Expects Q3 and Q4 volumes stronger than Q2; H2 typically 20% higher than H1.
items.quote: Based on our current indication, we expect Q3 and Q4 volumes to be stronger than Q2. Overall volumes and historically also H2 is always 20% up on H1.

items.statement: Exports expected to be 45% higher this year than previous year.
items.quote: Year-on-year, we expect this year to be 45% higher than our previous year.

items.statement: Seamless tube facility production trials planned for February or March 2027.
items.quote: The sizing mill and straightening mills have been received and installed, and we plan to undertake production trials in February or March of 2027.

items.statement: Total seamless tube capex budget INR170 crores; INR120 crores spent as of Q2.
items.quote: the total budgeted cost is approximately INR170 crores, okay? Out of this is funded by INR110 crores via term loan. The rest is from internal accruals, okay?

items.statement: Plans INR60 crores immediate capex via warrants and pref shares over next two quarters.
items.quote: close to INR60 crores we are planning on an immediate capex via warrants and pref shares, which we would be spending between the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Further INR50 crores capex on seamless tube in H2; total H2 capex about INR110 crores.
items.quote: we are looking at a further balanced capex of close to INR50-odd crores out of the INR170 crores, which is there.

items.statement: Backward integration into seamless tubes expected to add 3-4% margin on overall business.
items.quote: on the overall business, we should be having a margin of approximately 3% to 4% once we use our own seamless tubes for it.

items.statement: Seamless tube cost expected 8-10% lower than existing buying prices.
items.quote: it should be at around approximately 8% to 10% lesser than -- or you could say more competitive than existing buying prices.

items.statement: Price revisions with OEMs and Tier 1 customers to support Q3 and Q4.
items.quote: the price revisions, including -- concluded with the OEMs and Tier 1 customers are expected to support us during the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Steel prices increasing each quarter; OEMs and mills discussing another increase in Q3.
items.quote: steel as a commodity, we see increase going on in each and every quarter. I do believe that OEMs and mills are also talking about another increase in quarter 3 as well.

items.statement: Agri segment momentum to continue in Q3; tractor production planned at 13,000-14,000 in Oct-Nov.
items.quote: We expect this momentum to continue into Q3, supported by relatively lower inventory levels of tractors in the market.

items.statement: Extruded axle beam production at 80% of current output; to reach 100% by Q3 or Q4.
items.quote: Commercial production of our extruded axle beam has commenced and the capacity utilization of this is approximately 80% of our current output.

items.statement: Preferential issue of INR63.6 crores to fund expansion initiatives.
items.quote: The company is completely focused on capacity expansion and gearing up for the coming years, which is also witnessed by a preferential issue to the tune of INR63.6 crores.

items.statement: Difficult to guide on return to 14-15% EBITDA margins due to cost escalation and settlement pressures.
items.quote: Yes, it is difficult currently. The companies are facing a lot of pressures in terms of escalation and then the settlements and everything.

items.statement: H2 FY27 EBITDA growth expected in mid-to-high teens, with FY27 better than initial guidance.
items.quote: So we expect a very strong closing for the year and we definitely stay true on the guidance, that yes, H1 has been far stronger than the guidance and we expect the trends to continue but definitely mid-to-high teens (EBITDA) for the balance of the year is something that we are anchored towards.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 RevPAR growth expected in double digits.
items.quote: We see a lot of pick up happening around the long festive weekends that are there in the months of October and November. So we are very much on track for double -digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well.

items.statement: Effective tax rate anticipated to be in the 20s in FY27.
items.quote: We anticipate an effective tax rate to be in 20s in FY27.

items.statement: Capex for five contracted pipeline hotels is around INR 1,432 crores, with INR 150 crores spent.
items.quote: So, I'll tell you the capex for our five contracted pipelines, is Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh is around INR1,432 crores. We have spent around INR150 crores.

items.statement: Planned capex spending: around INR 450 crores by end of this year, INR 600 crores next year.
items.quote: By the end of this year, we will be spending around INR450 crores. Next year, we are looking at spending around INR600 crores, and subsequent to that, the balance capex.

items.statement: Mumbai BKC project capex remains INR 800 crores, split equally between equity and debt.
items.quote: There is no change in the overall capex cost as of now. The INR 800 crores of our committed capex remains the same; INR 400 crores of equity and INR 400 crores of debt.

items.statement: Contracted to over 5,200 keys by FY30, with about 2,600 under ownership.
items.quote: Our goal currently, we are already contracted, and at various, including our openings that we are at various stages of development, at over 5,200 keys by FY30, and which will include 2,600 or so keys, which will be under our ownership.

items.statement: Excluding ESOP and Coorg, flow-through was around 60% for the quarter.
items.quote: Excluding the ESOP cost, the EBITDA margin will be even better. The flow-through, excluding ESOP and exclud ing Coorg because Coorg is also stabilizing and it's not giving the EBITDA numbers as Jaipur and Udaipur, flow-through would be around 60% for the quarter.

items.statement: Management fees flow down to 85% to 90% into EBITDA for new managed openings.
items.quote: So, yes, for a new managed opening, if you get a management fees, it flows down to 85% to 90% into the EBITDA.

items.statement: Corporate rate negotiations targeting mid-to-high double-digit growth for CY27.
items.quote: So we are pitching for mid -to-high double-digit growth rates in terms of our ask rates , but the negotiations are on.

items.statement: International business grew low double-digit last quarter, expecting return to 50-50 mix.
items.quote: International business has also started slowly trickling in. In the last quarter, there was a low double-digit growth in terms of international business (even excluding BRICS).

items.statement: Suite occupancy rose over 700 basis points, with paid suite occupancy in mid-40s.
items.quote: If you look at our portfolio, our suite occupancy has risen by over 700 basis points. That shows you how our guests are willing to pay for experience and quality.

items.statement: Dubai asset operating at breakeven EBITDA, with renovation planned for early FY28.
items.quote: We are looking at taking the hotel under renovation in early '27, I would say probably early FY28, to be precise, like April or so is when we to start the renovating hotel, and finish the renovation within a year.

items.statement: Seeking shareholder approval for incremental fund infusion to buy FSI for BKC project.
items.quote: Since this is a material transaction with a related party, with the JV entity, Leela will shortly reach out to the shareholders for an approval of investment.

items.statement: Borrowing costs reduced by 30 basis points from mid-October through lender renegotiation.
items.quote: Additionally, our borrowing costs have reduced by a further 30 basis points from mid -October, as we have actively renegotiated with our lenders, which provides a shield from potential transmission of policy rate hikes.

items.statement: Raw material basket expected to increase 4-5% in Q3 FY27
items.quote: And our guidance going ahead for Q3 would be a further increase of about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: NSR increased 7% QoQ in Q2; planning further 4-5% increase in Q3
items.quote: And going ahead in Q3, we are planning a further increase in our NSR of 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Expect some margin improvement in Q3 despite raw material cost pressures
items.quote: So I see that some basic points going forward in Q3, definitely, there would be some improvement in terms of the margins.

items.statement: Balance capex for FY27 around Rs 500 crore after Rs 800 crore spent in H1
items.quote: This is going to be roughly around INR500 crores for the balance period.

items.statement: New expansion of Rs 1,130 crore underway; further phased capex of ~Rs 5,000 crore planned
items.quote: we are now taking up expansions immediately for INR1,130 crores, which is going on and then thereafter in phases for around INR5,000 crores capex.

items.statement: JK Tornel expects normal sales comparable to last year by Q4 FY27
items.quote: we are hoping that we will come back to the normal sales, which would be comparable to last year's sales.

items.statement: Demand steady in Q3; Q4 expected to be strong due to OEM year-end closing
items.quote: We see the demand being steady in Q3. And Q4, as we know, that will be the year-end closing for most of the OEMs also, there will be good demand coming in.

items.statement: Premium SKUs (16 inch & above) account for nearly 30% of passenger line volumes in H1 FY27
items.quote: At JK Tyre, nearly 30% of passenger line volumes sold in H1 are towards premium SKUs i.e. 16 inch & above tyres.

items.statement: West Asia conflict driving raw material inflation; cumulative 30% increase in last 6 months
items.quote: Cumulatively, we have seen a staggering 30% increase in the last 6 months.

items.statement: EV volumes surged 24% QoQ; leadership in electric truck & bus segment
items.quote: we are proud to share that our EV volumes have surged by 24% over the previous quarter.

items.quote: Domestic markets recorded a healthy volumes growth of 22%, driven by a robust 25% in OE Market and a similar 20% in replacement markets.
